stem: A parent asks why a child’s ADHD medicine may need to be adjusted over time rather than following a fixed formula for every child; which statement best explains this approach?

options.text: The choice of drug depends on clinician preference and the child’s response
One stimulant is always superior for every school-aged child
Medication choice is determined only by whether the child is a boy or girl
Drug selection should be based only on a single behaviour rating scale
Once started, ADHD medicines should never be reconsidered

explanation: The choice of drug depends on clinician preference and the child’s response. ADHD medication selection is individualised and should be reviewed over time to match the child’s clinical response and needs.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because ADHD medicine choice is individualised and guided by clinician preference and the child’s response.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because there is no single stimulant that is always best for every school-aged child.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because sex may affect presentation, but it does not solely determine medication choice.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because rating scales can inform assessment, but they do not by themselves determine drug selection.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because ADHD medicines should be reviewed and adjusted according to response and tolerability.
